e: Zonula occludens (tight junction) seals paracellular space via claudins/occludins, blocking free diffusion between cells.
Superior temporal gyrus (Wernicke's) lesion → sensory aprosodia (can't comprehend emotional tone).\nInferior frontal gyrus (Broca's) → motor aprosodia (flat, monotone speech).
Neuropraxia = reversible physiological conduction block c̅ axon & nerve sheath intact (mildest Seddon grade).
Neurapraxia = physiological conduction block, axon & sheath both intact — recovers fully once block resolves.
Parietal lobe integrates vision + somatosensation → hand-eye coordination & spatial awareness.
Inguinal ligament is the rolled-under free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis.
Right main bronchus is wider, shorter & more vertical (in line c̅ trachea) → foreign bodies lodge here more often.

Levator veli palatini: arises from the cartilaginous part of Eustachian tube and blends c̅ the soft palate, elevating it.
Tensor veli palatini: hooks around the hamulus, opens the tube.
Thyroid = endoderm, adrenal medulla = neural crest cells, kidney = intermediate mesoderm.
Ileum → Peyer's patches; transverse colon → taenia coli; oesophagus → non-keratinised stratified squamous; duodenum → villi (c̅ Brunner's glands).
Tailgut cyst = remnant of the embryonic postanal hindgut, seen in the retrorectal/presacral space.

Parotid is a purely serous gland (serous acini only).
Sublingual is predominantly mucous.
Midline cleft lip = midline upper-lip/philtrum defect from the medial nasal process (intermaxillary segment).
Marked structure articulates with the occipital bone.
Foramen ovale transmits the mandibular nerve (V3) – motor supply to muscles of mastication.
Correct pairing: 4-A (inferior colliculus), 3-B (superior cerebellar peduncle)

Tensor veli palatini (V3) mainly opens the Eustachian tube.
Stylopharyngeus, palatopharyngeus, constrictors (CN IX/X) drive swallowing & speech.

Lateral pterygoid (opens mouth, protrudes mandible) attaches to the neck of mandible/TMJ capsule.
Medial surface of ramus = medial pterygoid.
Pudendal nerve, internal pudendal vessels & ischiococcygeus relate to this region; obturator externus tendon does not.

1st arch → maxillary a.; 2nd → hyoid & stapedial aa.
3rd → common carotid; 4th → right subclavian (right side).
Image 4 : Acini + intralobular ducts + septa = exocrine (salivary gland) \nRest all are Ductless
Septum pellucidum separates anterior horns the two Lateral ventricles.
Bone D gives passage to a nerve arising from the brain (cranial nerve).
The muscle acting on both hip & knee extension arises from structure B.
Ulnar n. supplies hypothenar muscles (ADM), all interossei and medial 2 lumbricals (3rd & 4th).
Action of the muscle at the marked attachment: depression.
CN XII is purely motor to the tongue - no role in smell; CN I is the main olfactory nerve (V, IX, X carry irritant/chemosensory input).
Piriform recess is supplied by the internal branch of superior laryngeal n. - afferent limb of the cough reflex.
Gluteus medius/minimus (marked) = hip abductors; stabilise pelvis in single-leg stance.
Dura of posterior cranial fossa (C2-C3, vagal branches) → referred pain to back of neck/occiput.

Calot's triangle: cystic duct, common hepatic duct, inferior liver edge.
Cystic artery is a content, not a boundary.

Superficial peroneal n. (L5, S1) → peroneus longus & brevis (evertors).
Peroneus tertius & EHL = deep peroneal n.
Snuffbox tenderness after FOOSH = scaphoid fracture (risk of AVN of proximal pole).
INO = MLF lesion: failure of adduction in ipsilateral eye c̅ nystagmus in abducting eye; convergence preserved.
Orbicularis oris is the muscle reconstructed in primary cleft lip repair (restores lip continuity/function).
Ureter passes beneath the vas deferens ('water under the bridge'); seminal vesicles lie on the bladder base lateral to the vas.
LA receives pulmonary veins; pulmonary trunk lies anterior to ascending aorta; aorta arises from LV; RV hypertrophies in pulmonary stenosis.
Endocrine cell cluster (islet) releases hormones locally to neighbouring cells = paracrine signalling.
